# Count Twice: certified payroll checker

> A free page that checks one week of certified payroll before the contractor signs it. You drop in a CSV file and type each trade's base rate, fringe and apprentice ratio from your wage determination. It flags pay under the base rate, short fringe, overtime under 1.5 times the basic rate, and apprentices over the ratio. It runs in the browser: nothing is uploaded or saved. Made by Kerr & Company LLC, Grand Rapids, Michigan. Facts checked 8 November 2026.

## What it checks
- Base rate plus fringe on every hour, paid as cash, plan payments or both (29 CFR 5.31, 40 U.S.C. 3142(d))
- Overtime over 40 hours in the week at 1.5 times the basic rate, with the fringe at its straight amount (40 U.S.C. 3702, 29 CFR 5.32)
- Apprentices over the program's ratio on any day (29 CFR 5.5(a)(4))
- Rows it can't read, and trades with no rate typed
- A Michigan mode for state projects that counts the overtime hours on Michigan rate schedules

## What it doesn't check
- Whether each worker is in the right trade, or whether you have the right wage determination
- Gross pay, deductions and net pay
- Apprentice pay steps, and whether each apprentice is registered
- Hours worked off the job in the same week
- Due dates, and other states' prevailing wage rules

It checks math against the rates you type. It isn't legal advice, and the contractor still signs the Statement of Compliance.

## Pages
- [Count Twice: certified payroll checker](https://counttwice.app/): the checker, how to use it, what it checks and doesn't, and Michigan's online certified payroll, which started 2 April 2026
- [How to fill out the WH-347, line by line](https://counttwice.app/wh-347/): every box on the January 2025 form (OMB 1235-0008), a filled-in row with overtime and cash fringe, page 2's Statement of Compliance, and when and where it goes
- [Davis-Bacon wage rates for 2026](https://counttwice.app/davis-bacon-wage-rates/): finding a wage determination on SAM.gov, reading its rate identifiers, which modification applies, and the Executive Order notes, with Kent County, Michigan as the example
- [What is prevailing wage?](https://counttwice.app/prevailing-wage/): how DOL picks the prevailing wage (majority, 30 percent, weighted average) with a worked example, federal against Michigan's Act 10 of 2023 side by side, and why DOL's state table is out of date
- [The Davis-Bacon Act](https://counttwice.app/davis-bacon-act/): the $2,000 coverage test, the related acts, who counts as a laborer or mechanic, what a contractor owes each week, and what short pay costs
- [What is certified payroll?](https://counttwice.app/certified-payroll/): who files on federal and Michigan state jobs, the 7-day federal and 10-day Michigan deadlines with a worked week, where each payroll goes, what the signed statement means, the 3-year records, and what follows when it's late or wrong
- [California prevailing wage](https://counttwice.app/california-prevailing-wage/): California public works pay: the $1,000 test, DIR's February and August rate sets, daily overtime with a worked week, the $400 contractor registration, monthly certified payroll to the Labor Commissioner, and the apprentice floor
- [New Jersey prevailing wage](https://counttwice.app/nj-prevailing-wage/): the $19,375 municipal and $2,000 thresholds, where the county rate files are, $500 contractor registration, daily and Saturday overtime with a worked week, and certified payroll through the Wage Hub within 10 days
- [Sample week](https://counttwice.app/sample-week.csv): a CSV file with every column, and made-up names and rates
- [Privacy](https://counttwice.app/privacy.html)
- [Terms](https://counttwice.app/terms.html)
